detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.21618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety cases are widely used to demonstrate that mission-critical systems, such as autonomous vehicles and unmanned aerial systems, can operate safely after deployment. However, manually constructing safety cases is complex, time-consuming, and labor-intensive, which calls for the proposal of automated approaches to support their creation. Inspired by the legal nature of safety case construction, we formalize the safety case creation problem through a courtroom analogy, where stakeholders collaboratively propose, examine, criticize, review, improve and validate safety claims and their supporting evidence. In this analogy, the safety analyst acts as a prosecutor by identifying hazards and safety concerns, while the assurance case developer serves as a defense attorney by constructing and substantiating safety arguments. An orchestrator acts as a judge by coordinating stakeholder interactions, and a review board serves as a jury by assessing argument completeness and persuasiveness. Based on this formalization, we propose eTrustWare, a Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent framework for automated safety case generation and review. Our experiments on several safety cases of ML-enabled autonomous driving systems demonstrate the feasibility of coordinated LLM-based agents for generating safety cases.
